messages:
Tess (AE): FYI team — PromiseWorks (enterprise fintech) sent a 120-question RFI + capability matrix. Deadline EOD Friday. They want: technical answers, security questionnaire, POC scope, and a pricing tier view. I uploaded the doc to the sales drive: /shared/promiseworks/rfi/promiseworks_rfi_v1.xlsx. Can we break this up?

Priya (SE): I can take the technical + capability matrix. Will triage which questions need engineering input. Quick Q: do they require on-prem or VPC? I saw both options in the intro.

Tess (AE): They listed both, but preference is VPC w/ BYOK. On-prem only if VPC isn't acceptable. Also asked about HSM-backed key storage.

Sam (Security): I'll own the security questionnaire. I grabbed the spreadsheet — looks like the standard 40-ish security items plus PCI/SSO/HSM follow-ups. I'll draft answers for the high-risk items and flag anything needing Legal.

Alex (Sales): I'll handle pricing tiers / POC commercial. Need to know expected QPS and embedding vs. generation split to size Dedicated / burst. Priya — can you estimate token throughput for their sample workload?

Priya (SE): Sure. I skimmed the sample prompts. Two modes: high-concurrency short embeds (~512 tokens total per request) and occasional long-generation (avg 1.2k tokens). Rough back-of-envelope: if they have 200 concurrent embed qps -> ~100k embed/sec tokens — needs Dedicated pool sizing. I'll put exact numbers in a small table.

Priya (SE): Also, for capability matrix rows around "structured output enforcement" and "function calling", we should call out Redwood's streaming + function/tool calling as available on Hosted and Dedicated; Private supports it but requires runtime >= 2.1 and extra firewall ports. I'll paste suggested wording below.

Priya (SE): ```Suggested capability answer: "Function/tool calling and structured response enforcement — Supported. Hosted and Dedicated provide first-class streaming + function call semantics. Private deployments support the feature with runtime >= 2.1 and a connectivity allowlist (ports 443 + 8443 for control plane egress). We recommend pinning model variant and enabling token-level monitoring during rollout."```

Sam (Security): For the security spreadsheet, I'll answer standard items (SOC2, TLS1.2+, encrypted at rest). Two questions to escalate to Legal: export controls section and contractual indemnity wording referencing third-party model licenses. Jordan, can you review once I flag?

Jordan (Legal): Yep — ping me on the specific Qs. Also confirm whether customer data residency commitments are required (they're a EU/US hybrid).

Tess (AE): They asked for an on-site audit option in the RFI (one line). We should propose a hosted + remote audit as default and an on-site as paid add-on — cheaper for them to start remote. Alex, include that in pricing.

Alex (Sales): Will do. Proposed POC: 4-week evaluation using Redwood Dedicated reserved burst with an option to test Private in week 3 if they need BYOK. POC pricing: ~$Xk for 4 weeks baseline + add-on for HSM/onsite audit. I'll draft a POC SOW snippet and attach it.

Priya (SE): POC SOW snippet (paste): ```- Week 0: infra prep & access (VPC peering, IAM, KMS proof-of-concept)
- Week 1-2: ingest + perf baselines (embedding QPS + generation latency targets)
- Week 3: security verification + optional Private smoke test
- Week 4: handoff + runbook and performance report```

Tess (AE): Nice. Also they asked about failover behavior if Dedicated capacity is exhausted. Recommended wording?

Priya (SE): Recommend: "Smart routing with automatic fallback to a lower-cost compatible model or alternate region (configurable by customer). Customers can pin rollouts to avoid fallback for strict SLA requirements." Keep short.

Sam (Security): I've started answering security Qs. A few samples:
- Q: "Do you provide customer-managed HSM support?"
- A: "Yes — Private deployments support customer-managed KMS/HSM via supported integrations (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, on-prem HSM appliances). Dedicated supports BYOK for encryption at rest; for HSM-backed signing workflows we recommend Private."

Sam (Security): Another flagged Q: "Where are logs stored and who has access?" I'll answer: "Logs are retained in the customer-controlled project/tenant for Private; for Hosted we provide tenant-level logs with role-based access controls and optional log export to customer S3/GCS. Access is restricted to authorized SRE/Support with audit logging."

Alex (Sales): Attachments to prepare for submission: capability_matrix_filled.xlsx (Priya), security_q_answers.docx (Sam), poc_sow_v1.pdf (Alex), pricing_sheet.csv (Alex). Upload location?

Tess (AE): Put everything in the same drive folder: /shared/promiseworks/rfi/final_submission/. I'll create a zip after approvals.

Priya (SE): Quick note for the capability matrix on quantization — PromiseWorks asked about int8 support for our inference runtime. Suggested short answer: "Quantized model variants (int8) are supported on Dedicated and Private with validated profiles; Hosted may offer select quantized flavors based on compatibility — we'll surface availability per model in the catalog."

Sam (Security): There are two PCI-related checkboxes. We don't claim PCI attestation for Hosted by default. Proposed answer: "We support PCI-compliant deployment patterns (Private + Dedicated with hardened controls) and can provide guidance on cardholder data flows. For a formal PCI attestation we will need a scoped engagement." Flagging for Jordan.

Jordan (Legal): Flag received. I'll draft a short escalation paragraph for the submission that clarifies attestation timeline and any assumptions (no cardholder data stored on Hosted etc.).

Tess (AE): Deadline reminder: draft bundle to me by Thursday 5pm PT so I can review and send Friday morning. Who can do review-by-Thursday?

Priya (SE): I can have the matrix and technical writeups by Thu 12pm PT.

Sam (Security): Security QA by Thu 3pm PT. I'll mark any legal escalations in-line.

Alex (Sales): Pricing + POC SOW by Thu 4pm PT.

Jordan (Legal): I'll review flagged legal items Thu 4:30pm PT.

Tess (AE): Great. One final ask from them: "sample SLA for Dedicated with burst" — Priya, can you paste our standard SLA blurb?

Priya (SE): SLA blurb (short): "Redwood Dedicated SLA: 99.95% availability for reserved pools, with defined remediation and credits. Burst capacity subject to capacity availability; automatic fallback to hosted-compatible variants to preserve availability. Specific SLA terms depend on contract and committed capacity."

Tess (AE): Perfect. I'll assemble and run final pass. Also @deploy-bot — can you create a folder snapshot link for the drive path when we're ready?

deploy-bot: Folder snapshot created: https://drive.internal/s/promiseworks/rfi/final_submission/ (will update when files are uploaded) :white_check_mark:

Tess (AE): Thanks everyone. I'll collect drafts and post a checklist in the folder. If anything high-risk pops up, thread here and @Jordan for legal. :thumbsup:
